headline: Google DeepMind says Gemini 4 is almost ready, aiming for launch much earlier than year-end
summary: Google's new DeepMind chief, Koray Kavukcuoglu, stated that the frontier AI model is in its refinement stage, with an early release planned "much earlier" than the end of 2026.
details: Google's new DeepMind chief, Koray Kavukcuoglu, announced that the Gemini 4 AI model is nearing launch. He stated that the model is currently in its refinement stage and the company aims to release it "much earlier" than the end of 2026.

Kavukcuoglu expressed excitement about the results seen so far, indicating an intention to release an early post-training output as soon as possible. He also confirmed Google's commitment to "fast-paced iterations" going forward.

This news follows a period where Google has reportedly lagged behind competitors in flagship AI releases, with its last major model, Gemini 3, launched in November 2025. Rivals like OpenAI's GPT-6 and Anthropic's Mythos series have since launched, outperforming Gemini 3.

Google had previously announced a Gemini 3.5 Pro update for June, which was never rolled out. Kavukcuoglu explained that the company instead focused on developing faster, less powerful Flash models. Despite falling behind, he asserted confidence that Google "will always gonna be at the frontier" of AI.

headline: Detecting and Stopping Rogue AI Malware: Real Threats & Quick Fixes Explained
summary: Rogue AI agents are a fast-moving cyber-threat blending LLM power with classic malware. Recent reports show a spike in AI-driven ransomware and phishing bots, necessitating immediate detection and mitigation.
details: Rogue AI agents are no longer a sci-fi plot device—they’re a concrete, fast-moving cyber-threat that blends the generative power of large language models (LLMs) with the stealth of classic malware. In the past month, Hacker News, r/netsec, and several security newsletters have been flooded with reports of AI-driven ransomware, phishing bots, and self-modifying payloads, prompting a sharp spike in searches for "AI bot malware" and "LLM-enabled threats."

For SOC analysts, DevOps engineers, and security leads, a hands-on playbook is crucial to spot, contain, and eradicate these agents before they pivot to critical assets. This guide details the anatomy of a rogue-AI attack, provides ready-to-run detection snippets, and offers a concise mitigation checklist.

The article includes concrete, copy-and-paste commands for endpoint detection platforms, SIEMs, or quick Bash/Python probes. One example flags any source IP sending over 5 KB payloads to an LLM endpoint within a minute as high-risk.

A self-contained Python script (approximately 30 lines) is also provided, which can be run on any host to flag suspicious LLM traffic in real time. It is recommended to save it as detect_rogue_ai.py and schedule it with cron or a Windows task.
